posts.title: Hello, world
posts.excerpt: Why I'm starting a notes section, what to expect, and how it fits into the macOS-portfolio fiction.

content.text: This is the first entry in what I plan to keep as a working notebook — half engineering log, half growth-marketing diary. The frame is a Mail.app-style reader because that's where I read most of my own incoming long-form, and a portfolio that pretends to be a desktop should have a place to read.
Three things I want to write about here over the next few months:

items: **Agent SDK & MCP work** — building reproducible workflows on top of Claude Code, and what breaks when you scale them.
**Growth analytics, in code** — turning the playbooks I ran at 2K and Atlas Primer into queryable, shippable systems.
**Self-hosted infra notes** — the Hetzner / Cloudflare / Docker stack that runs my projects, and the small lessons that don't make it into README files.

content.text: If something here is useful, the canonical home is `andriybabiy.com/desktop` → Blog. Everything else is a mirror.

posts.title: A mobile metaphor for a desktop portfolio
posts.excerpt: When the metaphor is macOS, what should mobile look like? Notes on swapping Springboard in instead of redirecting away.

content.text: The /desktop route on this site is a macOS Sonoma reconstruction — top bar, dock, draggable windows, the whole metaphor. Until today it didn't render gracefully on mobile. The temptation was to redirect phones back to the canvas home page.

I went the other way. Below 768px the same route now renders an iOS Springboard: status bar, 4-column app grid, home indicator, fullscreen sheets in place of windows. Same apps, same data, different metaphor.
Why not just shrink the desktop?

items: **Pointer vs. touch.** Dock magnification and draggable windows are pointer-driven. They do not survive a thumb.
**Discoverability.** iOS Springboard is a metaphor users already have a model for. Free affordances.
**Consistency of fiction.** If the bit is "your portfolio is an OS," the OS should know what device it's on.

content.text: The implementation is one viewport hook (`useViewportMode`) that picks one of two trees. The app components themselves — About, Projects, Contact, Blog, the PDF viewer — are unchanged; they render inside a Window on desktop and inside a fullscreen sheet on mobile.
